segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ גֵּץ שֶׁיָּצָא מִתַּחַת הַפַּטִּישׁ וְהִזִּיק – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «a spark that emerged from under the hammer» of a blacksmith and started a fire, «causing damage,» the blacksmith is «liable» for the damage caused.

segments.he: גָּמָל שֶׁהָיָה טָעוּן פִּשְׁתָּן, וְעָבַר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְנִכְנְסָה פִּשְׁתָּנוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַחֲנוּת וְדָלְקָה בְּנֵרוֹ שֶׁל חֶנְוָנִי, וְהִדְלִיק אֶת הַבִּירָה – בַּעַל גָּמָל חַיָּיב. הִנִּיחַ חֶנְוָנִי נֵרוֹ מִבַּחוּץ – הַחֶנְוָנִי חַיָּיב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּנֵר חֲנוּכָּה – פָּטוּר.
segments.en: In the case of «a camel that was laden with flax and was passing through the public domain, and its flax extended into a store and» the flax «caught fire from a lamp» in the store «belonging to the storekeeper, and» as a result of the burning flax the camel «set fire to the building» together with all its contents, «the owner of the camel» is «liable.» But if «the storekeeper placed his lamp outside,» thereby causing the flax on the camel to catch fire, and consequently the building was set on fire, «the storekeeper» is «liable. Rabbi Yehuda says: In» a case where the lamp placed outside was «a Hanukkah lamp,» the storekeeper is «exempt,» since it is a mitzva for a Hanukkah lamp to be placed outside.

moves.summary: Camel owner liable when flax catches fire in a store
Storekeeper liable if lamp was placed outside

moves.about: whether a storekeeper whose lamp placed outside ignited flax is liable when it was a Hanukkah lamp

positions.claim: The camel owner is liable, unless the storekeeper placed his lamp outside, in which case the storekeeper is liable
If it was a Hanukkah lamp the storekeeper is exempt
